title: Skate or Die!
build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

records.c: 6510 data direction register. Named only because the KERNAL copy loop at $038E leaves its self-modified page operands wrapped round to $00 ($0390/$0393 count $E0..$FF, then $00); the loop never reads or writes $0000 itself

6510 processor port. The boot writes $35 at $09E6 (BASIC and KERNAL ROM out, I/O in: from then on the KERNAL calls run from the RAM copy made at $0389) and stage 3 writes $25 at $2026 just before loading the title (KERNAL still out); the title starts with $25

Stage 1's pointer $02/$03 (wiped code, see facts.md): the end of the running-XOR decryption ($0CD1, set at $0CD4), then the end of the packed drive routine ($0F06, set at $05CC), and last the start of the wipe: $0CBA sets $03 = $04 with $02 still $06, so the wiper at $EF00 clears $0406-$1005 and leaves $02/$03 = $06/$10
High byte of boot_ptr: the page counter of the wiper at $EF00, which stops when it reaches $10
Resident loader: current load address, $90 low and $91 page, from X/Y at load_setup ($F295) and advanced a page per sector ($F258). Stage 3's load of file $00 left it at $5200
Page of ldr_addr
Resident loader: end address, $92 low and $93 high = load address + the file's length from file_table; returned in X/Y. After stage 3's load of file $00: $51FF
High byte of ldr_end
Resident loader: the track of the next sector of the file (from file_table +0, advanced by next_sector)
Resident loader: the sector of the next sector of the file (file_table +1 made physical by logical_to_physical, advanced by next_sector)

Receive end flag: incremented at $F625 when the receive pointer $EF/$F0 reaches the limit $F1/$F2; from then on bytes are still taken from the drive but not stored ($F604). Cleared by read_sector_cmd ($F42E)

Index of the byte within the sector being received, 0-255: cleared by send_drive_command ($F4BF), stepped at $F628; when it wraps the sector is complete. In link mode bytes 0 and 1 are the next track and sector

Shift register of the command byte while send_drive_command clocks it out: $E2 (command), $E4 (track byte) and $E3 (sector byte) are shifted as one 24-bit number, command first, most significant bit first ($F505-$F50B)
Shift register of the sector byte (copy of $E7), the last 8 of the 24 bits sent
Shift register of the track byte (copy of $E6), the middle 8 of the 24 bits sent
The drive command for send_drive_command: 1 read sector, 3 data, 4 write sector, 5 reset buffer, $0B disk ID, $0C status, $80 drive reset. Commands below 3 expect a reply
Track byte of the command (for command $0B the first ID character). In link mode the receive code replaces it with the sector's link track ($F5ED); 0 there ends the chain
Sector byte of the command. In link mode the receive code replaces it with the sector's link sector ($F5F6)

Receive mode: 1 = raw, every byte of the sector stored and no chaining (read_sector_cmd sets it); 0 = link mode, the first two bytes are taken as the next track/sector and the reply chains on to it ($F635-$F644). The resident code never sets 0; the boot's own copy of this loader did, to load stage 3
Receive shift byte: $DD00 with bit 6 inverted, shifted twice so that the data bit (CLK line) lands in carry ($F5B0-$F5C7)
The byte being assembled from the drive, one bit per handshake, rotated in at $F5CA
Receive pointer $EF/$F0: where the next stored byte goes (set by set_dest_ptr, stepped at $F60D even when nothing is stored)
High byte of ldr_dest; its top nibble also seeds xfer_state when a reply is expected ($F53F)
Limit pointer $F1/$F2 (set by set_end_ptr): when ldr_dest reaches it, ldr_end_flag is set and storing stops. The byte at the limit is not stored
High byte of ldr_limit
Sectors completed in the current transfer (cleared by read_sector_cmd, stepped at $F62D). While it is 0 in link mode, bytes 2 and 3 of the first sector (a load address) are skipped ($F5FF)
Set while wait_transfer is running ($F561, cleared at $F573) so that bg_receive does nothing meanwhile
Byte budget of one receive_bytes call: decremented per byte at $F598, the call returns when it reaches 0 (bg_receive loads it from bg_slice_bytes)
Set to $FF at the end of every received sector ($F632). Nothing in memory reads it
write_sector's index into the 256 bytes it sends two at a time (command 3); write_sector has no caller

The last instructions of the EA file (loaded by the KERNAL at $0102-$01FD), still in the stack page: the end of the loop that fills $0100-$01CB with $01, erasing EA's own code, then JMP $0CD4 into stage 1, which EA has just read from track 1 sectors 7-20 into $0334-$1133. The loop starts at $01C8 (LDY #1, TYA, DEY), which the fill has already overwritten

The rest of EA: $01D7-$01FD alternate $01 and $00. The KERNAL's LOAD returns with RTS through this stack area, pulls $00/$01 and lands at $0101, the byte just before the file; after a cold start BASIC's number output leaves $38 there (the '8' of 38911 BYTES FREE), a SEC, and the processor runs on into $0102 (simulated with KERNAL 901227-03, work/agent-boot/autostart.js). Stack pushes during the game have overwritten the part from $01E9

Stage 1 file (track 1 sectors 7-20, read by EA to $0334-$1133) begins with JMP ($FFFC). Nothing jumps to $0334 except the cartridge test at $03A8; the KERNAL ROM is still mapped then, so the vector is the KERNAL's own and the machine resets. $0334-$0339 lie before the decryption range ($033A-$0CD1) and are stored in clear

$0337 and $0338: zero bytes that seed two integrity checks of stage 2. $03D3 XORs $0337 with $0100-$011F (32 bytes of $01 left by EA's wipe, so the result is 0 only if EA ran) and wants 0; $03E2 XORs $0338 with $03EF-$0422 and wants $3E. $0339 = $EA, the seed of the running XOR at $0CD4

Three-byte checksum built by $0D18 (wiped): every third byte of $03D5-$0419 XORed into $033A, $033B and $033C in turn. The boot carries on only if they end as $1E $62 $B8, which they hold here; otherwise $0D50 jumps to the wipe-and-return at $0CAE with nothing pushed, which crashes
X saved by the M-W sender at $062F (wiped) while it sends one byte of the drive routine
The key of the XOR layer being applied by decrypt_layer: the low byte of its caller's return address

Stage 2's layered decryption: XOR $03BF-$0953 (5 pages plus $95 bytes) with one key, the low byte of the caller's return address, read with PLA/PHA so the return is not disturbed. It is called from $03BF (key $C1), $03D0 ($D2), $03F7 ($F9) and $0472 ($74): each call undoes one layer just ahead of the code that follows the call and scrambles again what has already run. No moment holds all of stage 2 in clear; work/agent-boot/stage12-exec.txt lists each instruction as it was when it ran
Pointer to stage 2's entry, $0389: the target of JMP ($0344) at the end of stage 1's decryption ($0D14). It sits inside decrypt_layer, which jumps over it (BEQ $0346)
decrypt_layer's loop: Y runs 0-255 over the five pages $03BF, $04BF, $05BF, $06BF and $07BF, and over $08BF-$0953 while Y < $95, each byte XORed with the key kept in $033E; returns when Y wraps

Stage 2 entry (from $0CD4's JMP ($0344)), with interrupts off: copy the KERNAL ROM to the RAM under it ($E000-$FFFF, 32 pages, the page operands at $0390/$0393 self-modified); write 0 to $8003 and read it back, and if it is not 0 (a cartridge's ROM mapped at $8000) jump to $0334 and reset; point the NMI and RESET vectors in RAM at $0954 (an RTI, so RESTORE does nothing); build the EA logo screen at $0982 (wiped), which also banks the ROMs out ($01 = $35); CLI. The first decrypt_layer call follows at $03BF

High byte of LDA $E000,Y: the source page, stepped from $E0 by INC $0390 after each page (with the store's page at $0393); after 32 pages both have wrapped to $00. The copy reads the KERNAL ROM and writes the RAM beneath it, since a write to a ROM address always reaches RAM
High byte of STA $E000,Y, stepped with $0390 by INC $0393. Then the cartridge test at $03A0, the NMI/RESET vectors at $03AB, JSR $0982 (logo screen, ROMs out) and CLI: see stage2_start

The rest of stage 2's first page, $03BF-$03FF, as the last decrypt_layer pass left it: not valid code. Decrypted at run time it is the integrity checks, the drive-routine upload ($05C4) and the drive commands: see facts.md
Six bytes of stage 2 ($0400-$0405, scrambled) that survive the wipe because the wiper starts at $0406 ($02 is still 6 from the drive-routine decoder)

Stage 3, the last boot program, loaded by stage 2 from the chain track 3 sectors 0-5 (each byte XORed with $A5 as it arrived) to $2000-$25F1 and entered by the RTS of the wiper at $EF00. It copies the resident loader image $2100-$25FF to $F230-$F72F (5 pages), sets the processor port to $25 (BASIC and KERNAL ROM out, I/O in), loads file $00 at $4000 with load_file and jumps to it: the title program

Bytes $2034-$20FF of the stage 3 file: never executed and never read (the read map of the simulated boot has no access here). They look like bitmap or sprite bytes left in the assembler's memory when the file was saved; meaning unknown

Resident loader image, copied by stage3_install to $F230-$F72F. This page becomes $F230-$F32F: load_file, save_file, load_setup, next_sector, logical_to_physical and the first rows of file_table. Identical to the copy except where the copy has since modified itself ($F4B3/$F4B5)
Resident loader image, the page that becomes $F330-$F42F: file_table rows $0E-$30, sectors_per_track, track_interleave, xfer_state and the first command routines

Resident loader image, the page that becomes $F430-$F52F: write_sector, set_disk_id_cmd, drive_query_status and send_drive_command (its operands $2383/$2385 are still 0 here; the copy's were patched by the title load)
Resident loader image, the page that becomes $F530-$F62F: the end of send_drive_command, wait_transfer, bg_receive and receive_bytes

Resident loader image, the page that becomes $F630-$F72F: the end of receive_bytes ($2500-$2523 = $F630-$F653), then the bytes after the end of the stage 3 file in its last sector ($2524-$25F1, an orphaned fragment of some other program that calls $167F and reads $24E0) and 14 bytes of the power-on pattern the load never reached ($25F2-$25FF). All of it is copied
Cartridge test byte: stage 2 writes 0 here at $03A2 and reads it back at $03A5; ROM mapped at $8000 would return its own byte. RAM here, so the 0 is still in place

The EA logo screen (VIC bank 3, screen $C000, characters $C800: $DD00 bits 0-1 = 0, $D018 = $02), built by stage 2 at $0982: cleared to character 0, colour RAM all $0F, then 256 bytes copied from $0A04 to $C148 and 256 from $0A0C to $C150. The logo is 7 rows by 22 columns at rows 8-14, columns 9-30, characters $01-$30. Border $0F light grey, background $06 blue at first; stage 2's receive code adds 1 to $D021 at each new page it stores, six times while it loads stage 3, so the background ends at $0C, medium grey. Still on screen when the title starts
The EA logo's character set: 49 hires characters, $00 blank and $01-$30 the pieces of the logo, copied by stage 2 at $09C1 from $0B0C (256 bytes to $C800) and $0B94 (256 bytes to $C888, overlapping)

The wipe-and-return, copied with the 256 bytes from $0CC3 to $EF00 by $0CAE and entered with A = 0: store A through boot_ptr from $0406 up to $1005, erasing stages 1 and 2, then RTS. Stage 2 has pushed $1FFF before jumping to $0CAE, so the RTS enters stage 3 at $2000. On a failed integrity check the same RTS returns to whatever is on the stack

The rest of the page $0CAE copied, $0CD4-$0DC2, which at that moment held track 3 sector 0 as stage 2 had read it raw (each byte XORed with $A5): $EF11/$EF12 the link to track 3 sector 1 ($A6 $A4, the link bytes XORed too), $EF13/$EF14 the load address $2000 that stage 2 took from $0CD6/$0CD7, and $EF15-$EFFF the first 235 bytes of stage 3, the same as $2000-$20EA. Never executed here

RESIDENT LOADER, load entry (JMP $F236). Call with A = file number ($00-$30, file_table $F2F9) and X/Y = load address (lo/hi). Returns carry clear and X/Y = the end address (one past the last byte), or carry set on a drive error. High Jump calls it at $0806 (stub), $08F8, $094E, $0959 and $123F (JMP); it chains files by passing the end of one as the start of the next ($0951). Uses zero page $90-$95 and $E0-$FB
Second loader entry (JMP $F26A): write a file's sectors to disk, same A and X/Y as load_file. Nothing in this snapshot calls it

load_file proper: load_setup (also sends the disk ID), then per sector: end pointer to $F1/$F2 (set_end_ptr), destination page to $EF/$F0 (set_dest_ptr), read_sector_cmd with track $94 and sector $95, wait_transfer for the 256 bytes, next_sector; the page $91 goes up by one each time until $90/$91 reaches the end $92/$93. Only the bytes before the end are stored (the drive still sends whole sectors)
save_file proper: the same sector walk as load_file_body, but each sector goes out through write_sector ($F43A) from the pages at X/Y. No caller in this snapshot

Set up a file transfer: $90/$91 = X/Y (start), $92/$93 = start + length from file_table, $94 = start track, $95 = start sector (made physical by logical_to_physical when the track's interleave is 11). Then sends drive command $0B with $45 $41 (set_disk_id_cmd), which tells the drive to expect disk ID "EA"; a disk with another ID fails its reads

Advance $94/$95 to the next sector of a file: sector = (sector + track_interleave[track]) mod sectors_per_track[track]; when that comes back to 0 every sector of the track has been used and the walk moves to the next track at sector 0, stepping over track 18 (the directory track)
A = file_table start index; returns A = index*11 mod the sector count of track Y, the physical sector that is the index-th in the interleave-11 sequence (0, 11, 1, 12, ... on a 21-sector track)

Resident loader file table, 4 bytes per file, files $00-$30 (49 entries): +0 start track, +1 start sector as an index into that track's interleave sequence (converted to a physical sector at $F2E4), +2/+3 length in bytes (lo/hi). Files $00-$1A are on side 1, $1B-$30 on side 2 (both start again at track 3). Read by load_setup ($F295). Checked: files $0B, $0C, $0E, $0F, $11 and $12 read from side1.g64 with this table equal the snapshot, apart from the bytes of $0B the game writes at run time
file_table +1 column: start sector index of each file (the auto symbol of the indexed read at $F2B4)
file_table +2 column: file length low byte, added to the load address X to make the end pointer $92 ($F29C)

file_table rows from +3 of file $00 to file $0F: length high byte added to Y for $93 ($F2A3). Notable rows: file $0B (track 12) is the resident event manager loaded at $F730; file $0C (track 18 sector 18, 3 bytes) is the disk-side ID; file $0E (track 14, $34FF bytes) is High Jump's first part at $0880; file $0F (track 17, $200 bytes) the font High Jump loads to $6800
file_table, from the +3 byte of file $0E on: the first byte of the loader's second page, where stage3_install's copy of $2200 begins (the auto symbol comes from its STA $F330,X)

file_table rows for files $10-$1F: $10 (track 17, $17D9 bytes, loaded by High Jump to $4000), $11 (track 19, $1284 bytes, to $7000), $12 (track 20, $402C bytes, loaded straight after $11, ending at $C2B0); $13-$1A are other side-1 files; $1B (side 2, track 3, $3780 bytes) is the file event 3 (DOWNHILL) loads
file_table rows for files $20-$2F, all on side 2 ($28, track 14, $378D bytes, is the file event 4 (JAM) loads)
file_table row for file $30 (side 2, track 25 index 14, $09A2 bytes), the last entry; the sectors-per-track table follows
Sectors per track, indexed by track 0-35 (entry 0 unused): 21 for tracks 1-17, 19 for 18-24, 18 for 25-30, 17 for 31-35. Read by next_sector ($F2CE) and logical_to_physical ($F2ED)

Sector step per track, indexed by track 0-35: 1 on tracks 1-3, 18 and 35, 11 on all others. next_sector adds it modulo the track's sector count; load_setup multiplies the start index by 11 when it is 11 or more ($F2B2)

Loader transfer state: 0 = idle or finished, $80 = failed (set with carry at $F648), any other value = a sector transfer is pending (set at $F54A to the destination page high nibble, or $10; only zero, negative and positive are ever tested). Written $F4C2/$F54A/$F4AB/$F650, read by wait_transfer ($F553) and bg_receive ($F57E)
Bytes per call for bg_receive ($F57E) plus one: $14, copied to the countdown $F9 there. Read only at $F58A
Status byte returned by drive command $0C, stored by drive_query_status ($F4A5); nothing in this snapshot reads it
Three bytes ($C0 $F3 $CF) that nothing in this snapshot reads by name; reachable only by an out-of-range track index into track_interleave
Store X/Y as the receive pointer ldr_dest $EF/$F0 (absolute addressing of zero page) for the next transfer
Store X/Y as the limit pointer ldr_limit $F1/$F2: receive_bytes stops storing when ldr_dest reaches it
Send command $80 (bit 7 set): the drive's command server takes any such command as JMP ($FFFC), a reset of the drive back to its own DOS. No caller in memory

Ask the drive for one sector: command 1 with track Y and sector X, raw mode (ldr_raw_mode = 1: every byte stored, no link bytes followed); clears ldr_sector_count and ldr_end_flag. Through send_drive_command
Operand high byte of STA $00E0 in read_sector_cmd: the first byte of the loader's third page, where stage3_install's copy of $2300 begins. The routine is described at $F421

Write one sector: command 5 (resets the drive's buffer index), 128 commands 3 each carrying two bytes read from ($EF/$F0), then command 4 with track Y and sector X (patched into $F47C/$F477), which writes the drive's buffer to disk, then wait for the drive's one-byte reply. No caller in memory
Operand of an LDA # in write_sector: the sector for the final command 4, patched from X at $F43A
Operand of the second LDA #: the track for command 4, patched from Y at $F43D

Send command $0B with track byte Y and sector byte X; the drive's command server stores them as the expected disk ID (drive zero page $12/$13). load_setup sends $45 $41, "EA", before every file, so the title load began with it
Send command $0C and receive the one byte it answers (the drive's last job status) into drive_status_byte $F407. No caller in memory
Mark a reply pending (xfer_state = $10) and fall into wait_transfer
Operand of the LDX # at $F4B2: send_drive_command's caller X, patched at $F4B7 and handed back on both exits ($01 here: the sector of the title load's last read, track 4 sector 1)
Operand of the LDY # at $F4B4: the caller's Y, patched at $F4BA ($04 here, the track of that read)

Send the 3-byte command in $E5 (command), $E6 (track byte), $E7 (sector byte) to the drive's command server, keeping X/Y (saved into $F4B3/$F4B5, returned by the exit at $F4B2, entered at $F4B1 with carry set on failure). It sets $DD00 bit 3 (ATN), fails with carry set if bit 7 (DATA in) is already high or bit 6 (CLK in) does not go low and then high within 255 polls (the drive toggles CLK while ATN is held), clears bit 3, then clocks out 24 bits most significant first: each bit on $DD00 bit 4 (CLK out), strobed by pulsing bit 5 (DATA out). For commands below 3 it marks a reply pending in xfer_state ($F54A). Returns carry clear when the command was taken. Stage 2 had its own copy of this code at $06B7, the same apart from zero-page addressing
Operand high byte of LDA $DD00 in send_drive_command's exit (release the bus lines): the first byte of the loader's fourth page, where stage3_install's copy of $2400 begins
wait_transfer's saved Y (written $F55B, restored $F579)
wait_transfer's saved X (written $F55E, restored $F576)

Wait until a pending reply has been received: if xfer_state is non-zero and positive, call receive_bytes until it is 0 (done) or $80 (failed, carry set). Sets the busy flag $F8 so that bg_receive does not run meanwhile; keeps X/Y ($F551/$F552)

Background receive: if no wait_transfer is running ($F8 = 0) and a reply is pending, take up to 19 bytes (count from bg_slice_bytes) and return, so a load can be spread over interrupts. No caller in this snapshot

Receive reply bytes from the drive while the countdown $F9 lasts: for each byte wait (up to $30 polls, else return) for $DD00 bit 7 to go high, then take 8 bits, each read as bit 6 of $DD00 inverted and acknowledged by a pulse on bit 5; bit 7 falling mid-byte means failure (xfer_state = $80). For command 3 and up the single byte is the whole reply. For a sector, raw mode stores each byte at ($EF/$F0) until the end pointer (end flag $E0); the other mode (not used by load_file) takes bytes 0/1 as the next track/sector link and asks for that sector itself ($F63F). After 256 bytes the transfer is done
Loop back to receive_bytes for the next byte of the sector (reached from $F62B while the in-sector count $E1 has not wrapped)
End of a sector in receive_bytes: flag ldr_sector_done, then in link mode chain to the next sector. Also the first byte of the loader's fifth page, where stage3_install's copy of $2500 begins

The tail of the loader image copied with it from $2524-$25FF: an orphaned code fragment from the end of the stage 3 file's last sector (it calls $167F and reads $24E0, neither of which exists in any boot stage), then 14 bytes of the power-on $00/$FF pattern. Nothing reads it; the event manager loaded later starts at $F730

NMI vector in the RAM under the KERNAL, $0954, written by stage 2 at $03AD. $0954 held an RTI, so RESTORE did nothing while the boot ran with the ROM banked out; the wipe has since zeroed it. The title starts with the KERNAL still out, so this vector is the live one

RESET vector in RAM, $0954, written with the NMI vector at $03B0. A hardware reset maps the ROM in before fetching it, so it is read only by the JMP ($FFFC) of the tamper exit at $097F (wiped), which then lands on the RTI at $0954
